title: Rangers pay tribute to Ralph Brand, a striker the goals still define
body:
Rangers have paid tribute to Ralph Brand, who has died aged 89 [S1]. The news was carried by BBC Sport [S1], and it has landed as a reminder of how much a club's history rests on the players who found the net.

The report places Brand among the most productive scorers the club has had [S1]. That is the lens that matters here. A striker is remembered first through his output, and framing the tribute around goals gets straight to why his name still carries weight with supporters.

There are no form lines or predictions to set against this story, so the judgement has to rest on the tribute itself. Nothing on the pitch changes the weight of a life's work, and nothing in the evidence suggests a wider storyline to chase.

That leaves the question of what comes next. A send-off is easy to write and easier to forget. The side that loses a legend owes its people more than a statement, and the real test is whether the goals keep being talked about once the messages have stopped arriving.

The Touchline Take: a fitting farewell, and the proper tribute is keeping the goals in the conversation long after the statements have faded.

evidence.text: BBC Sport: Rangers great Brand dies aged 89. Rangers have paid tribute to Ralph Brand, one of the most prolific goalscorers in the club's history, who has died aged 89.
